title: Finite purely inseparable extensions test geometric reducedness of any algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $C$ a commutative $k$-algebra. Tensor products carry their usual algebra multiplication [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The following are equivalent: (1) for every finite purely inseparable field extension $E/k$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], including $E=k$, the ring $C\otimes_kE$ is reduced; (2) for every field extension $K/k$, the ring $C\otimes_kK$ is reduced. Here reduced means that $x^n=0$ for $n\ge1$ implies $x=0$. No finite generation, Noetherianity, or reducedness hypothesis on $C$ is imposed, and the zero algebra is allowed.

source.place: Tag 030V, lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension, equivalence (1) and (5), with the definition of geometrically reduced expanded.

proof.text: Condition (2) immediately gives (1): each finite purely inseparable extension $E/k$ is a field extension, so apply (2) with $K=E$. The trivial extension $k/k$ is finite purely inseparable by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] (degree one, and each element already belongs to $k$). This also confirms that (1) includes the reducedness of $C$ itself via $C\otimes_kk\cong C$.

Assume (1). First fix a finitely generated field extension $F/k$, meaning $F=k(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ for a finite list of elements. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-make-separably-generated] to obtain fields $E,F\prime$ and a commutative square $k\to E\to F\prime$, $k\to F\to F\prime$, in which $E/k$ and $F\prime/F$ are finite purely inseparable and $F\prime/E$ is separably generated. In particular the two maps $k\to F\prime$ agree. Condition (1) applies to $E/k$, so $C\otimes_kE$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 030V, proof of (1) implies (5), the square supplied by Tag 04KM (lemma-make-separably-generated).

proof.text: Set $D=E\otimes_kC$. Swapping tensor factors, $c\otimes e\mapsto e\otimes c$, is a ring isomorphism with itself as inverse, so Step 2 makes $D$ reduced. Now [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced], applied over the field $E$ to its reduced algebra $D$ and the separably generated extension $F\prime/E$, makes $F\prime\otimes_ED$ reduced. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-cancel-base-change] with $R=k$, $S=E$, $A=F\prime$, $B=C$, the ring isomorphism $F\prime\otimes_E(E\otimes_kC)\to F\prime\otimes_kC$ sends $f\otimes(e\otimes c)$ to $ef\otimes c$, with inverse $f\otimes c\mapsto f\otimes(1\otimes c)$. Thus $F\prime\otimes_kC$ is reduced. The square in Step 2 ensures that its $k$-algebra structure is the one induced from $F\to F\prime$.

source.place: Tag 030V, proof of (1) implies (5), application of Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness); tensor cancellation is Tag 00D2 (lemma-tensor-with-bimodule).

proof.text: The $k$-module $C$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat]. The field map $F\to F\prime$ is injective; hence the defining condition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] makes $F\otimes_kC\to F\prime\otimes_kC$, $f\otimes c\mapsto f\otimes c$, injective. If $z^n=0$ in $F\otimes_kC$ for $n\ge1$, its image is zero by Step 3, and injectivity gives $z=0$. Therefore $F\otimes_kC$ is reduced. Swapping the two factors gives reducedness of $C\otimes_kF$ for every finitely generated field extension $F/k$.

source.place: Tag 030V, proof of (1) implies (5), descent from the square; injectivity spelled out using Tag 00HB (definition-flat).

proof.text: Let $K/k$ now be arbitrary and suppose $z^n=0$ in $C\otimes_kK$, $n\ge1$. By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], write $z=\sum_{i=1}^r c_i\otimes a_i$ and put $F=k(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\subseteq K$ (take $F=k$ if $r=0$). Lift this expression to $z_F=\sum_i c_i\otimes a_i$ in $C\otimes_kF$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] and the injectivity condition in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], tensoring $F\hookrightarrow K$ with $C$ is injective; swapping factors gives the injective ring map $j:C\otimes_kF\to C\otimes_kK$. Since $j(z_F^n)=z^n=0$, injectivity gives $z_F^n=0$. Step 4 gives $z_F=0$, hence $z=0$. Thus $C\otimes_kK$ is reduced for every field extension $K/k$, proving (2).

source.place: Tag 030V, proof of (1) implies (5), finite-generation reduction via Tag 00I3 (lemma-limit-argument), written directly for a finite tensor expression.

proof_origin.place: Tag 030V (lemma-geometrically-reduced-finite-purely-inseparable-extension), proof of (1) implies (5), with the finite-generation reduction and injective descent written out.
